finding: After vaginal delivery, but not cesarean delivery, the cumulative incidence of pelvic organ prolapse, stress incontinence, and overactive bladder is associated with pelvic muscle strength, but the associations attenuate when adjusting for genital hiatus and body mass index.
mod_finding: After vaginal delivery, but not cesarean delivery, weaker pelvic floor muscle strength was associated with a shorter time to develop pelvic floor disorders.
followup_time: 5-10 years after first delivery at enrollment, with annual follow-up for up to 9 years
